defect_summary: GovernanceService.list_review_queue() returns raw store items with no evidence-ref redaction. The two BFF routes that serve it directly from governance/router.py -- GET /api/v1/operator/governance/review-queue and the /bff/reviews compatibility alias over the same data -- never called redact_evidence_refs()/capabilities_for_identity() on review_summary.evidence_refs, so a caller lacking a required capability (e.g. metric.read, job.read) received every evidence ref unredacted. BFF-FINAL-007 (commit 4a14129b9) originally enforced this redaction on the review-queue endpoint in main.py; the seam extractions BFF-MAIN-COMPOSITION-SEAM-EXTRACTION-002 (eea73dd09) and BFF-MAIN-FINAL-SEAMS-CORRECTIVE-001 (3f88e5fa7) moved the endpoint's implementation out of main.py into governance/router.py + governance/service.py without carrying the redaction call forward.

fix_summary: services/control-plane/bff/governance/router.py: added a _redact_review_queue_items(identity, items) helper that deep-copies each review-queue item, redacts review_summary.evidence_refs through the existing _safe_redact() closure (which already wraps the injected canonical redact_evidence_refs from models.py and capabilities_for_identity from auth/policy.py, exactly as wired by core/app_factory.py), and sums a redacted_evidence_count. Wired this helper into list_governance_review_queue (GET /api/v1/operator/governance/review-queue), bff_list_reviews (GET /bff/reviews), and bff_get_review (GET /bff/reviews/{review_id}) -- all three serve the same underlying GovernanceService.list_review_queue()/get_review() data and would otherwise leave the /bff/reviews* compatibility surface as a trivial bypass of the review-queue fix. No changes to models.py, auth/policy.py, core/app_factory.py, governance/service.py, human_inbox.py, management_read_models/service.py, incidents/service.py, or main.py -- the canonical redaction policy owner and its wiring were already correct; only the two/three route handlers were missing the call. Redaction fails closed: _safe_redact already treats a capability-lookup failure as an empty capability set, so every capability-gated ref is withheld rather than disclosed.

pagination_regression_repair.defect_summary: The fix above redacted/counted the entire filtered (unpaged) review-queue result before _paged() selected the returned page: list_governance_review_queue and bff_list_reviews called _redact_review_queue_items(identity, items) on the full filtered list, then passed the already-redacted list into _paged(). Both routes therefore returned only the current page's items but reported meta.redacted_evidence_count for the whole filtered queue, not the returned page. Reproduced with a two-item store (item 1 alert-only, item 2 metric+job): GET /api/v1/operator/governance/review-queue?page_size=1 and GET /bff/reviews?page_size=1 both returned item 1 (zero redacted refs) with meta.redacted_evidence_count=2.
pagination_regression_repair.fix_summary: In services/control-plane/bff/governance/router.py, reordered list_governance_review_queue and bff_list_reviews to call _paged(items, ...) first (on the raw, unredacted, filtered list) and then run _redact_review_queue_items(identity, response["items"]) only on the page actually returned, overwriting response["items"] and computing meta.redacted_evidence_count from that page alone. page_info.total is still computed by _paged() from the full filtered list length, so pagination totals are unchanged. Availability projection is preserved: when the dataset surface is unavailable, _paged() already returns page_items=[] before redaction runs, so redacted_evidence_count correctly reports 0 for a withheld page instead of counting refs that were never returned.
